questions.title: Taking away leaves and sticks
questions.question: You see some leaves and little sticks next to your ball on the fairway. What can you do?

choices.text: You can move them away and don’t get a penalty
You can move them, but you get a penalty
You have to leave them there
You can only move them if your friend says yes

questions.explanation: You are allowed to pick up and move leaves and little sticks near your ball on the fairway. You do not get a penalty for this.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Things like leaves, twigs, or stones that are not stuck down and can be moved.
The short grass area between the tee and the green where you hit the ball.

questions.teachingTip: Let children try removing leaves and stones from next to a ball in practice, so they get used to what a loose impediment is and how to do this safely.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think they cannot touch anything near the ball.
Some may believe they always need an adult or friend’s permission to remove leaves or twigs.
Children might think they will always get a penalty for moving things around their ball.

questions.title: Moving loose impediments
questions.question: You find some leaves and twigs touching your ball on the fairway. What can you do according to the rules?

choices.text: You can remove them but will get a penalty
Only remove them after asking your marker

questions.explanation: Loose impediments like leaves and twigs may be removed anywhere on the course, including the fairway, without penalty.
